newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BNZ sees tight margins but positive environment.
newsitem.headline: BNZ sees tight margins but positive environment.

text.p: Bank of New Zealand Ltd, a unit of National Australia Bank, said on Thursday it expected the 1996-97 operating environment to be positive overall but there were likely to be some challenges.
"We believe margins will remain tight and the industry competition intensify," Managing Director Gordon Wheaton said after BNZ announced a 5.3 percent rise in annual net profit to NZ$318 million.

"There could be some impact from the political situation as New Zealand comes to grips with the new MMP environment and we expect underlying inflationary pressures to come from sources such as wages, house prices and easing fiscal policy, but we see good growth conditions bringing an increase in demand for lending in the household sector," Wheaton said.
MMP or Mixed Member Proportional is the new electoral system which has produced drawn-out coalition negotiations, so far with no clear outcome, since a general election on October 12.
"We would see lower interest rates and more certainty in the political scene contributing to an upturn in investment and credit demand from the business sector as well," Wheaton said.
